preamble: Place assimilation of the moraic nasal to a following velar consonant (/k, ɡ/), yielding the velar nasal [ŋ] (palatalized [ŋʲ] before palatalized velars). The moraic nasal /N/ (ん) of Japanese is phonologically placeless and is conventionally written /ɴ/ after its traditional pre-pausal description, though real-time MRI work (Maekawa 2023, JIPA 53(1), https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100321000050) shows that even utterance-final /N/ ranges from uvular to alveolar closure depending on the preceding vowel. Okinawan has the same moraic nasal, also transcribed /ɴ/, with the same assimilation (its isolation form is velar [ŋ̍]). No language outside Japonic is documented with a uvular nasal that assimilates in this way; elsewhere [ɴ] is usually itself an allophone of /n/ or /ŋ/ before uvulars.

examples.note: /ɴ/ before the voiced velar stop /ɡ/ surfaces as [ŋ].
The moraic nasal before velar and labiovelar consonants is realized as syllabic [ŋ̍].
